title: SEBI’s F&O curbs cut retail losses below Rs 1 lakh crore but average loss per investor still remains high
description: Retail F&O losses fell to Rs 91,685 crore in FY26 from Rs 1.12 lakh crore after SEBI’s regulatory measures, while the number of individual investors and trading turnover also declined.

Retail F&O losses fall below Rs 1 lakh crore: What SEBI’s curbs changed. Retail investors’ aggregate net losses in the equity derivatives segment fell to Rs 91,685 crore in FY26, down from Rs 1.12 lakh crore in the previous financial year, following regulatory measures introduced by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI), Parliament was informed on Tuesday. Minister of State for Finance Pankaj Chaudhary, in a written reply to the Rajya Sabha, said the number of unique individual investors in the equity derivatives segment also declined year-on-year to 78.60 lakh in FY26 from 98.10 lakh in the previous fiscal. While the overall losses fell, the average loss per individual investor increased to Rs 1,16,654 from Rs 1,13,913 during the period. F&O trading volumes also decline The decline in retail participation was accompanied by a fall in overall trading activity in the equity derivatives market. Equity derivatives turnover declined to Rs 202 lakh crore in FY26 from Rs 213 lakh crore in FY25, according to the minister. Chaudhary said the decline followed a series of measures undertaken by SEBI from November 2024 to strengthen the F&O segment and improve risk management. These included rationalising weekly index derivatives products, increasing tail-risk coverage on options expiry days, raising the contract size for index derivatives and rationalising monthly index derivative products. SEBI also introduced upfront collection of option premiums from buyers, removed calendar spread treatment on expiry days and began intraday monitoring of position limits. In May 2025, the capital market regulator also introduced further measures to streamline expiry days across exchanges and implement risk metrics for position limits to improve monitoring and disclosure of risks in the F&O segment. STT collections rise sharply Despite the decline in trading turnover, Securities Transaction Tax (STT) collected from F&O trades across the NSE and BSE rose sharply. According to the minister, annual STT collections from F&O trades increased to Rs 27,695 crore in FY26 from Rs 7,893 crore in the previous year. The data comes amid continued regulatory efforts to curb excessive retail participation and losses in the equity derivatives segment, particularly in options trading. Loss-making companies can still launch IPOs In a separate reply, Chaudhary said companies reporting losses or negative net profits are permitted to launch initial public offerings (IPOs) in India. As per information furnished by stock exchanges to SEBI, 39 companies with negative net profits or accumulated losses were listed on the mainboard stock exchanges over the last five years. The government’s response comes as regulators continue to focus on investor protection and risk management across India’s capital markets.
